note: miniOrange module that secures REST/JSON:API by registering a Drupal authentication_provider (RestAPI, id rest_api_authentication, priority 150). When enable_authentication=1 the provider applies() to /jsonapi/ and ?_format= requests and validates credentials by method: 0 basic_auth, 1 api_key, 2 oauth, 3 jwt, 4 external_oauth (oauth/jwt/headless-sso/multi-app are premium). All state is the rest_api_authentication.settings config object (enable_authentication, authentication_method, api_token, applications map, default_application_id, plus miniOrange customer fields). Runtime authentication of a real HTTP request and any miniOrange/external OAuth call is out of scope for the eval env, so EVERY case is grounded in the local config/auth-provider only: medium reads whether protection is on / which method the default app uses; hard turns protection on and sets the expected api_token - all verified by drush cget, no external auth. Install baseline sets only customer_* fields; the enable/applications/api_token keys are absent until configured, and cleanup clears them back to that baseline.

evals.prompt: How does the REST & JSON API Authentication module secure a Drupal site's API, which requests does it protect, and what single setting turns that protection on?
evals.expected_output: It registers a Drupal authentication provider (RestAPI, id rest_api_authentication, priority 150). When enable_authentication=1 in rest_api_authentication.settings, the provider applies() to requests whose URI contains /jsonapi/ or ?_format= and requires valid credentials; normal page requests are untouched.

evals.prompt: Which API authentication methods does the REST & JSON API Authentication module support for validating incoming API requests?
evals.expected_output: Basic Auth (method 0), API key (1), OAuth (2), JWT (3), and external OAuth (4). Basic Auth and API key are in the free version; OAuth/JWT/external OAuth (and headless SSO / multiple applications) are premium miniOrange features.

evals.prompt: On a Drupal site with the REST & JSON API Authentication module, in which configuration object are its settings stored, and which key is the master on/off switch for API protection?
evals.expected_output: All settings live in the rest_api_authentication.settings config object; enable_authentication (0/1) is the master switch that activates the authentication provider.

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, is REST/JSON:API authentication protection currently active? Inspect the live configuration to answer.
evals.expected_output: Yes - protection is enabled: rest_api_authentication.settings has enable_authentication = 1, so the auth provider protects /jsonapi/ and ?_format= API requests.

evals.prompt: On this site, the REST & JSON API Authentication module has a default API application configured. Inspect the live configuration and tell me which authentication method that default application uses.
evals.expected_output: The default application (app-eval-1) uses the API key method: its authentication_method is 1, which maps to api_key (rest_api_authentication.settings applications + default_application_id).

evals.prompt: On this Drupal site, turn on REST & JSON API Authentication so that unauthenticated /jsonapi and ?_format REST requests are no longer served. Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: Set enable_authentication = 1 in rest_api_authentication.settings (via the auth settings form or drush config): \Drupal::configFactory()->getEditable('rest_api_authentication.settings')->set('enable_authentication', 1)->save();

evals.prompt: Configure REST & JSON API Authentication so that the API-key method expects the token 'EVAL-TOKEN-9x'. Apply the change to the live configuration.
evals.expected_output: Set api_token = 'EVAL-TOKEN-9x' in rest_api_authentication.settings (the api-key method compares the presented token against this): ->set('api_token', 'EVAL-TOKEN-9x')->save();
